title: Mango and Coconut, Same Fruit? Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
A juicy mango and a hard, hairy coconut look nothing alike. Diya spotted both in the kitchen and asked: how can these two be the same kind of fruit? The answer is hiding in the layers of the fruit wall.

You will see that a fruit is a ripened ovary and a seed is a ripened ovule, with banana as a parthenocarpic fruit. A zoom ladder goes into a mango: the pericarp, then epicarp, mesocarp and endocarp, then the stone with the seed inside. A flower turns into a fruit in five animated steps. Then a gram seed (testa, tegmen, hilum, micropyle, cotyledons, radicle, plumule) and a maize grain (endosperm, aleurone layer, scutellum, coleoptile, coleorhiza) are labelled and compared, followed by a pause and think on the coconut, a worked example sorting six parts, the mango stone exam trap, an original statement question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself. This is Episode 46 of our PUC Biology series.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE), PUC (Karnataka) and NEET students.
